entry.title: How we built a sanctions screening API that outperformed the Federal Reserve's benchmark
entry.summary: The Federal Reserve published a sanctions screening We hit 100%. Here's how. 90-95% of sanctions screening alerts are false positives. The root cause: basic fuzzy matching. Most tools use 9 penalty layers targeting specific false positive patterns: Patronymic derivatives (Ivan ≠ Ivanov) Business-to-person mismatch Substring traps ("Computing" contains "Putin") Common name IDF weighting Mixed-script rejection Zero-width character evasion detection Normalization → smartNormalize() FAISS MiniLM semantic ANN search Jaro-Winkler + Monge-Elkan + Soft TF-IDF Double Metaphone phonetic blocking 9 penalty layers LLM cascade (40-85 confidence range) Adjudication engine 145 real test cases across 13 categories: OFAC, UN, EU, UK sanctions lists Arabic/Cyrillic transliteration Phonetic matching Substring traps Adversarial inputs Result: 145/145. 100% F1, 100% Recall, 100% Precision. The Federal Reserve tested organization names only, That's exactly what we tested. verifex.dev/benchmark Anyone can run it against any provider.
